name: Facet
text: We should default to a dark theme for our interface, as it will provide better visibility and reduce eye strain for users. This decision is supported by successful examples like Manus Competitive Analysis and Graphify Dashboard, which both utilize dark themes to enhance interactive data visualization. By choosing a dark theme, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially higher design complexity to ensure sufficient contrast and readability. This trade-off is worth it, as a well-designed dark theme will ultimately improve the overall clarity and enjoyment of our interface.

name: Pane
text: Dark themes don’t solve the real problem: users who need light mode for readability or accessibility. The risk is locking them into a single mode before we test—some may struggle with contrast or glare. Settle it by A/B testing a persistent light/dark toggle against a system-default dark theme, measuring completion time and error rates.
